headline_marked: Illegal sluice gate closures [[prolong flooding in Chattogram and Cox's Bazar]]
headline: Illegal sluice gate closures prolong flooding in Chattogram and Cox's Bazar
summary: Authorities say influential locals are blocking drainage gates to protect fish and salt farms, leaving hundreds of thousands of residents marooned.
details: Vast areas of southern Chattogram and Cox's Bazar remain submerged, with authorities blaming human-induced obstructions for worsening the flooding.
Officials state that influential people have closed sluice gates and built illegal embankments to protect fish enclosures and salt farms, preventing floodwater from draining into the sea.
The BWDB sluice gates are designed to open during low tide to allow floodwater to drain, but local groups have allegedly manipulated them for their own interests.
Tanzeer Saif Ahmed of the BWDB reported that some gates are being closed again immediately after officials reopen them.
In Chakaria, a journalist found a five-vent sluice gate almost entirely blocked by wooden planks to slow the current and protect fishing nets.
Local administrations and BWDB officials have spent several days cutting through these illegal barriers to restore water flow.
Pekua Upazila Nirbahi Officer Rafiqul Islam noted that these obstructions have caused prolonged waterlogging even in coastal unions that normally drain quickly.
